[Two outside awards support this work: an IMLS grant to UCLA and a Sloan Foundation grant to the multi-campus UC OSPO Network.]{.lede}

DSC's open source program office (<abbr class="term" title="Open Source Program
Office">OSPO</abbr>) work, licensing review, repository best practices, and release
guidance, is part of the UC OSPO Network, funded by a **{{< var software.sloan_amount >}} Sloan Foundation
grant** to the network as a whole (a multi-campus award, not a grant to DSC). It exists because the need is real: a 2025 scan of roughly
{{< var software.license_scan_n >}} UC-affiliated code repositories found
{{< var software.license_scan_pct >}} carried no license at all, meaning most UC
research code cannot legally be reused or built on.

Alongside it, a **{{< var software.imls_amount >}} IMLS grant** (Laura Bush 21st
Century Librarian Program, {{< var software.imls_grant_number >}}) funded an
open science curriculum built by and for librarians: 15 peer-reviewed lessons (14 were
proposed), each with a DOI, developed by two cohorts across 2023-2024. Tim Dennis served as Program Director, Todd Grappone as
Co-PI, and Zhiyuan Yao, DSC's GIS librarian at the time, as Program Coordinator. All
lessons are built on The Carpentries Workbench and released under CC-BY 4.0; one,
DMP 101, has already been formally adopted into the Library Carpentry curriculum,
with the rest in active community piloting.

That curriculum work sits inside a larger, ongoing commitment: Dennis co-chairs the
**Library Carpentry Governance Group**, which sets lesson-adoption and
curriculum-quality standards for the global Library Carpentry program, not just
UCLA's. DSC staff maintain or co-maintain lessons taught worldwide, from core
Carpentries material (Unix Shell, Tidy Data, R, Python, Computational Thinking) to
newer additions in qualitative data methods, data management, Wikidata, data
archiving, and AI, including a published lesson on using AI coding agents in
research while preserving validation and reproducibility
([agentic-research-workflows]({{< var links.agentic_lesson >}})). Dennis is also a
[Center for Open Science Ambassador]({{< var links.cos_ambassador >}}) (2016-present)
and was teaching faculty for the Berkeley Initiative for Transparency in the Social
Sciences' [Research Transparency and Reproducibility Training]({{< var links.bitss_rt2 >}}).
